'''Graham Kribs''' is an American theoretical [[particle physicist]] at the [[University of Oregon]]. He was elected a [[List of American Physical Society Fellows|Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2015.

== Early life and education ==
Graham Douglas Kribs was born in 1971, the son of Robert and Margaret Kribs.<ref name=":2" />

Kribs did undergraduate work at the [[University of Toronto]], and he participated in a Fermilab high energy physics program with Drasko Jovanovic. After that summer he "was hooked on high energy physics."<ref name=":1" /> He  earned a Ph.D. at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1998.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2019-12-09 |title=Graham Kribs - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/graham-kribs |access-date=2022-04-29 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> His dissertation, supervised by [[Gordon L. Kane]], was titled, ''Supersymmetric phenomenology, model building, and signals.''<ref name=":2">{{cite thesis |last1=Kribs |first1=Graham Douglas |date=1998 |title=Supersymmetric phenomenology, model building, and signals |id={{ProQuest|304434647}} |oclc=68800883 |hdl=2027.42/131252 |hdl-access=free |page=iii }}{{primary source inline|date=January 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
Kribs pursued studies at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Princeton, New Jersey]], between 2003–2005, and again in 2013.<ref name=":0" />

Kribs joined the University of Oregon Physics faculty in 2005 and was promoted to full professor in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Graham Kribs promoted {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://physics.uoregon.edu/2015/05/01/graham-kribs-promoted/ |access-date=2022-04-29 |website=physics.uoregon.edu}}</ref> He serves there as Director of the Institute for Fundamental Science, which "enhances the experimental, theoretical, and astronomy research activities at the University of Oregon."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute for Fundamental Science {{!}} Institute for Fundamental Science |url=https://ifs.uoregon.edu/ |access-date=2022-04-29 |website=ifs.uoregon.edu}}</ref> His research interests have included, "[[Physics beyond the Standard Model|new physics]], [[supersymmetry]], [[extra dimensions]] and [[black hole]]s".<ref name=":1" />
